frozen_original.synopsis: On December 3, 2022, Trump posted on Truth Social calling for the 'termination of all rules, regulations, articles, even those found in the Constitution' in order to reinstate him as president and nullify the 2020 election. The statement was widely condemned by constitutional scholars, Democrats, and even some Republicans as the most explicit anti-democratic statement a former president had ever made. Trump's own vice president Mike Pence said the remarks were 'wrong' and called on Trump to apologize. The episode was cited by January 6 Committee members as further evidence of Trump's contempt for constitutional governance. No significant disciplinary action or legal consequence followed.

frozen_original.title: Trump's DJT Truth Social Stock: Insiders Sell at Peak While Retail Investors Buy
frozen_original.synopsis: After Trump Media & Technology Group went public via SPAC merger in late March 2024, insiders including Trump himself held hundreds of millions of dollars in stock that retail investors bid up on political enthusiasm. As insiders were subject to lock-up periods, retail investors poured money into a company with negligible revenue and massive losses. Once lock-up periods expired, insider selling pressure drove the stock down substantially. The episode demonstrated how Trump's political celebrity was systematically monetized at the expense of ordinary investors who bought into the MAGA brand.

primary.title: Unverified Draft: Alleged Trump Media Insider Selling and Retail Purchases
primary.description_short: Internal draft: the claim that Trump Media insiders sold at a peak while retail buyers entered after the 2024 merger is unverified.
primary.description_medium: The frozen synopsis alleges that insiders sold Trump Media shares near a peak after the March 2024 SPAC merger while retail investors bought. The packet provides no transaction records or named sellers. Its Reuters link is summarized as reporting Trump said he would not sell when his lockup expired, which does not establish what others traded.
primary.description_long: The frozen synopsis alleges that, after Trump Media & Technology Group went public through a SPAC merger in late March 2024, insiders including Donald Trump held large share positions while retail investors bought the stock. It further claims that insiders sold near a peak after lockup restrictions expired, the price then fell, and Trump’s political profile monetized the MAGA brand at ordinary investors’ expense. These are supplied allegations, not verified findings. The packet provides no filings, seller identities, transaction dates or volumes, contemporaneous evidence of retail buying, or defined measure of the claimed price decline. Its supplied Reuters syndication reference is dated September 13, 2024, and is summarized as reporting that Trump said he did not intend to sell when his lockup expired. That source URL was not independently fetched in this run, and the supplied summary does not establish whether Trump or other insiders later sold. It cannot support a claim about other shareholders or prove investor losses or causation. The March 26 date is retained from the frozen record, not independently checked; peak timing, sales, buyers, losses and motives remain unknown.

frozen_original.title: DOGE accesses VA medical records without patient consent
frozen_original.synopsis: DOGE operatives accessed Veterans Affairs medical records without patient consent, exposing sensitive health information of millions of veterans in violation of federal privacy law. The unauthorized access to VA medical systems included records containing combat-related injuries, PTSD diagnoses, and other sensitive mental health information for millions of veterans. Veterans service organizations filed lawsuits demanding the data be secured, warning that the breach could expose veterans to discrimination and harm.

primary.title: VA Says DOGE Has Not Accessed Veterans' Personal Records Amid Privacy Concerns
primary.description_short: NPR reported uncertainty about a DOGE staffer's VA data access and the department's denial; the supplied claim of a completed breach is unsupported.
primary.description_medium: An NPR report published March 11, 2025, said a DOGE staffer had been present at VA while a current employee could not confirm what data the staffer could access. VA's spokesperson said DOGE had not accessed veterans' or beneficiaries' data, and the department's written reply to a Senate inquiry said DOGE had no access to veterans' personal records. The evidence documents concern and denial, not a confirmed breach.
primary.description_long: On March 11, 2025, NPR reported questions about DOGE's access to sensitive information held by federal agencies. For VA, NPR quoted a current agency employee saying a DOGE staffer had been present and that the scope of data access was unclear. The employee requested anonymity because of possible retaliation. A VA spokesperson told NPR that DOGE did not have and had not had access to veterans' or beneficiaries' data. In a written response to the Senate Committee on Veterans' Affairs about DOGE access to VA systems and sensitive information, VA likewise stated that DOGE did not have access to veterans' personal records. These sources support an access concern, the presence of a DOGE staffer, and an official denial. They do not establish that medical files were viewed, PTSD or combat-injury diagnoses were exposed, millions of records were accessed, or veterans' organizations filed lawsuits over a confirmed breach. The frozen card's breach language should be removed; its specific allegations remain unverified and contradicted by VA's statements.
